title: How ChatGPT makes you dumb (and how to use AI without paying cognitive debt)
summary: Ruben unpacks an MIT study showing passive ChatGPT use hurts recall and brain connectivity, then argues the fix is order: do the hard thinking first, invite AI second. He backs it with productivity data (BCG, GitHub) and six workflows that keep the human in the loop.

principles.text: Do the hard thinking first, then bring AI in second.
principles.quote: do the hard thinking first, invite AI in second

principles.text: Draft solo before prompting; use AI to challenge your structure, not write it.
principles.quote: Write a quick outline or even a rough first draft on your own.

principles.text: Treat AI as a booster, not the steering wheel; stay in the driver's seat.
principles.quote: You stay in the cognitive driver’s seat; the model becomes a booster, not the steering wheel.

principles.text: Top performers don't copy-paste AI output; they iterate and blend it with their own expertise.
principles.quote: They iterate, reframe, and blend the AI output with their own expertise.

principles.text: Use ChatGPT as a relentless critic that sharpens your reasoning instead of writing for you.
principles.quote: turn ChatGPT into a relentless critic that sharpens your reasoning rather than writing for you.

principles.text: Quiz yourself on AI-assisted work so the information actually sticks.
principles.quote: convert ChatGPT into a just-in-time memory trainer so new information sticks.
